export: Open the document, click File, then Download.
Choose a file type. The file downloads to your computer.

opensIn.note: Opens Word-type files (.doc, .docx) in Writer. Macros need rewriting.

google-docs.tip: Download as .docx (Word) if you are not sure; the Download menu lists the other file types.

export: Open the spreadsheet, click File, then Download.
Choose a file type. The file downloads to your computer.

opensIn.note: Opens Excel files (.xls, .xlsx) in Calc. Excel macros do not run unchanged.

export: Open the presentation, click File, then Download.
Choose a file type. The file downloads to your computer.

opensIn.note: Opens PowerPoint files (.ppt, .pptx) in Impress.

export: Go to Google Takeout (takeout.google.com) and sign in. Untick what you do not want.
Choose how to receive it (email link, or saved to Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive or Box) and a file type (zip or tgz).
Click Create export. You get an email when it is ready, usually within a day.
wontComeOver: Anything you change after you ask for the export is not in it.
The download link expires after about 7 days and works 5 times.
The page does not say what file format Drive files arrive in; Google Docs files are converted when you download them.

export: Go to Google Takeout (takeout.google.com) and sign in. Untick what you do not want.
Choose how to receive it (email link, or saved to Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive or Box) and a file type (zip or tgz).
Click Create export. You get an email when it is ready, usually within a day.
formats: Your photos and videos, plus separate JSON files holding extra data such as comments.
wontComeOver: Anything you change after you ask for the export is not in it.
The download link expires after about 7 days and works 5 times.
Album and date information can end up in separate files from the photos.

opensIn.note: Has a "Google takeout" import: download every zip part, then Upload > Google takeout in the desktop app. Reads the JSON files so dates and albums are kept.

google-photos.tip: Download every zip part before importing, and keep the originals until you have checked the new library.

export: On a computer (not the phone app), open calendar.google.com and go to Settings, then Import & export.
Under Export, click Export. You get a zip file of .ics files, one per calendar.
For one calendar: hover it in the left list, More, Settings and sharing, Export calendar.
wontComeOver: Work or school accounts may have export switched off by the administrator.
You need permission to manage a calendar to export it.

opensIn.note: Imports .ics files: Calendar settings > Import Calendar, pick one or more files, choose which calendar.

export: Go to Google Takeout (takeout.google.com) and sign in. Untick what you do not want.
Choose how to receive it (email link, or saved to Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive or Box) and a file type (zip or tgz).
Click Create export. You get an email when it is ready, usually within a day.
formats: Labels are kept inside each message as a header (X-Gmail-Labels).
wontComeOver: Anything you change after you ask for the export is not in it.
The download link expires after about 7 days and works 5 times.
You cannot export only a date range of Gmail.

export: Click Settings in the sidebar, then under Workspace choose General.
Click Export all workspace content.
Notion emails you a download link (it can take up to 30 hours; the link lasts 7 days).
wontComeOver: Only the current or default view of each database is exported, not every view.
Form views cannot be exported; export the responses from a table view.
Pages you cannot see (other people's private pages) are left out.
Callout blocks come out as HTML because Markdown has no equivalent.
notion.tip: On Windows, long folder names can stop the zip from opening. Untick 'Create folders for subpages' or extract with 7-Zip.

export: In the Evernote desktop app for Mac or Windows (not the web), select the notes or a notebook.
Choose Export and pick ENEX, single-page HTML, or multi-page HTML.
Save the file.
wontComeOver: Export works for up to 100 notes at a time or whole notebooks.
PDF export shows attachments only as pictures; choose ENEX or HTML to keep attachments as real files.
Evernote re-import does not preserve notebook structure (Evernote's page).

opensIn.note: Imports ENEX files and keeps notebooks. Scanned-document text is dropped unless OCR is on; some colours and fonts may not carry over.

export: On 1Password 8 for Mac: File > Export. On Windows/Linux: the ellipsis menu > Export.
Pick your account, enter your password, then choose 1PUX (keeps everything) or CSV (logins only).
On iPhone/iPad (iOS 26+): Settings > Advanced > Start Export. Passkeys can only leave from the phone apps.
wontComeOver: CSV leaves out security questions, linked items and custom fields such as backup codes. Use 1PUX to keep them.
Passkeys exported from a computer app are not included; make new ones on each site.
The exported file is NOT encrypted.

opensIn.note: Imports 1Password .1pux, .1pif and .csv files. File attachments must be re-uploaded by hand.

1password.tip: Delete the export file as soon as the import works.

export: In the web vault: Advanced Options > Export. LastPass emails a confirmation you must approve.
Or in the browser extension: Account > Fix a problem yourself > Export vault items; enter your master password.
wontComeOver: File attachments and trash must be added again by hand.
Sends (Bitwarden's) and some item types are not imported.

opensIn.note: Imports the LastPass CSV, or connects to your LastPass account directly from its extensions and desktop apps.

export: As a Workspace Owner or Admin, open the workspace export page (see the linked Slack help page for the menu path).
Choose the date range and start the export; Slack gives you a download.
wontComeOver: Free and Pro plans export public channels only; private channels and DMs need Business+ or Enterprise and approval.
Files come as links, not the files themselves.
Integrations, apps and workflows must be rebuilt.

opensIn.note: Imports a Slack export as a new organization: messages, reactions, users, channels and custom emoji. Threads become topics. Edit history and workspace settings do not carry over.
Imports a Slack export via its mmetl and mmctl tools: channels, DMs, threads, files, reactions. Custom emoji images, Canvases and integrations do not come over.

export: Open the board's menu, choose Print, Export, and Share, then pick the export option.
Premium Workspaces can export all boards as CSV or JSON from Workspace Settings > Export (admins only).
wontComeOver: Board JSON holds only the 1,000 most recent actions, so older comment history is cut off.
CSV leaves out comments and archived cards.
Inbox cards cannot be exported; move them onto a board first.

opensIn.note: Has Add Board / Import with Trello as a source; give it the Trello JSON file (a zip of several boards works too). No undo, so back up first.

export: Open Settings and privacy, then Account, then Your X data (or Download an archive of your data).
Confirm it is you with the code sent to your email or phone, then request the archive.
When X emails you, click Download while logged in and save the .zip.
formats: ZIP of HTML and JSON files: profile, posts, Direct Messages, media, followers
wontComeOver: Mastodon cannot import posts or media; only follows, lists, blocks and mutes in its own CSV format.
It may take a few days to prepare the archive.
twitter-x.tip: Follows can be moved if you first convert them to Mastodon's CSV format. Mastodon docs: https://docs.joinmastodon.org/user/moving/

export: Profile picture > Settings & privacy > Settings > Meta Account > Your information and permissions.
Click Export your information > Create export, pick your profile, then Export to device.
Choose what to include, date range, format (HTML to read, JSON to move) and media quality; click Start export.
formats: HTML (open index in a browser) or JSON, as a zip
wontComeOver: You have 4 days to download after the email arrives.

export: Use the Download your data tool on your Spotify Account Privacy page.
formats: A zip of data files with a 'Read Me First' file

export: Use Instagram's Download your information tool (the Help Center page names the steps).
Open the Bookmark Manager, open its More menu, choose Export Bookmarks.
Open the document and go to File, then Save a Copy (or Save As).
Click Browse and pick a folder.
In the Save as type list choose OpenDocument Text, name the file and click Save.
wontComeOver: Some formatting may be lost when saving as .odt.
Track Changes, document protection, macros, themes and watermarks are not supported in .odt (Microsoft's differences list).

opensIn.note: Opens Word files (.doc, .docx) in Writer. Word macros (VBA) must be edited to run.

microsoft-word.tip: Microsoft says to save a .docx copy first, then the .odt, so you keep your original.

export: Open the workbook and go to File, then Save As.
Choose where to save it, then in the Save as type list pick OpenDocument Spreadsheet (.ods) or CSV.
Name the file and click Save.
wontComeOver: Formatting might be lost when saving as .ods.
CSV and other text formats save only the active sheet and lose all formatting.
Standard .xlsx cannot store macro code; macros are in .xlsm and need rewriting in other programs.

opensIn.note: Opens Excel files (.xls, .xlsx) in Calc. With a few exceptions Excel macros cannot run unchanged.

microsoft-excel.tip: Reopen the .ods and compare it with your .xlsx before relying on it.

export: Go to File, then Save As.
Select Browse, choose a folder and name the file.
In the Save as type list choose OpenDocument Presentation (.odp) (it is at the end of the list), then Save.

opensIn.note: Opens PowerPoint files (.ppt, .pps, .pptx) in Impress.

export: In the desktop app open the page and choose File, then Export.
Under Export Current choose what to export, then PDF, and click Export.
For a whole notebook to move into Joplin, choose Notebook and OneNote Package (.onepkg) in the Windows desktop app.
wontComeOver: OneDrive's website cannot download a OneNote notebook as a zip: a folder holding one returns a zip with an error text file.
PDF export keeps the look but not editable notes.

opensIn.note: Imports OneNote through File > Import > ZIP - OneNote Notebook (needs Joplin 3.5.5 or later for desktop exports). .onepkg import works only when Joplin runs on Windows.

microsoft-onenote.tip: The .onepkg and .one routes come from Joplin's import page; the Microsoft page I could read only describes PDF.

export: In classic Outlook choose File, then Open & Export, then Import/Export.
Choose Export to a file, then Outlook Data File (.pst), then pick one account (tick Include subfolders).
Browse to a folder (not a OneDrive folder), name the file and click Finish. New Outlook: Settings, then Files, then Export, then Get started.
wontComeOver: Folder properties, message rules and blocked-sender lists are not exported.
By default Outlook holds only the past 1 year of mail on your computer; set the sync slider to All first, or you export only what is cached.
Only one account can be exported at a time.
microsoft-outlook.tip: Mozilla's community answers say Thunderbird has no built-in .pst import (it reads from an installed Outlook), so a converter is needed; I found no official page for it.

export: For personal-use Teams, sign in to teams.live.com/dataexport with your Microsoft account.
Choose Chat history, Media, or both, then select Submit request and Continue.
When it is ready, select Download.
formats: A .tar file holding messages.json and your files
wontComeOver: Chats arrive as a data file (messages.json), not as a conversation you can open in another chat app.
If you were removed from a community you cannot export its data.
These steps are for personal-use Teams; I found no official export steps for work or school accounts.

export: Open OneDrive on the web and open the folder.
Select everything (Ctrl+A) or select nothing to take the whole folder, then click Download.
Save the .zip file when your browser asks.
wontComeOver: OneNote notebooks cannot be downloaded this way.
Limits: 250 GB per file, 10,000 files per download.
Files protected by sensitivity labels over 4 MB are left out of the zip.

export: Open the file and choose File, then Save a Copy (or Save As).
In the format list choose Photoshop (PSD) to keep layers, effects and masks. TIFF can also keep layers.
For files over 2 GB use Large Document Format (PSB).
wontComeOver: Saving as PNG flattens layers and edits into one layer.
PSD files cap at 2 GB; PSD has no public spec, so other programs never read it 100% (Krita's manual).

opensIn.note: Opens and saves PSD: raster layers, blend modes, layer styles, groups, text and transparency masks. Transform masks are not loaded or saved; Krita 5.3 asks whether to load text as text or as a paint layer.

adobe-photoshop.tip: Krita's manual itself suggests .ora or .tiff over PSD when you can.

export: In Lightroom Classic select your photos and choose File, then Export.
Under file type pick Original to get each photo in its captured format (the Lightroom desktop app also offers JPG, TIF, DNG and Original).
Edits to raw files are stored in XMP sidecar files; turn on Automatically Write Changes Into XMP in Lightroom Classic so they exist.
formats: XMP sidecar files for raw photos
wontComeOver: Raw files keep their edits in a separate XMP sidecar; JPEG, TIFF, PSD and DNG get it written inside the file.
Edits carry over only partly: other programs read some data and need further adjustment.

opensIn.note: Reads Lightroom's .xmp sidecars on import: tags, color labels, ratings and GPS load; edits migrate only partly and often need adjusting. Use Add to library, not Copy & import, or the sidecar is ignored.

export: Save the project and make sure all media is linked.
Use the File menu's export options to export the project or sequence as Final Cut Pro XML.
Check the translation log file afterwards for conversion issues.
wontComeOver: Only a few Premiere effects and features transfer.
Audio pan, gain and level changes may not transfer accurately; complex effects and transitions may not translate exactly.
adobe-premiere-pro.tip: I could not verify from an editor's own docs that Kdenlive, Shotcut or OpenShot open this XML, so no alternative is listed.

export: Choose File, then Save As, and pick SVG for a file other programs can edit.
Or save the .ai file with Create PDF Compatible File ticked, so programs that read the PDF layer can open it.
Multi-artboard files: only the active artboard is saved to SVG.
wontComeOver: You cannot save each artboard as its own SVG.
Effects placed after an SVG effect turn the output into a raster object.
Illustrator-only data (layers, path effects, mesh gradients) sits in a stream Inkscape does not read; gradient meshes are approximated.

opensIn.note: Opens modern .ai files through its PDF importer; transparency modes do not work and gradient meshes are approximated. Older (PostScript) .ai files need picking the file type in File > Open.

export: Open the document and choose File, then Export.
Pick InDesign Markup (IDML) from the format menu and save.
wontComeOver: Not every InDesign object type is imported by Scribus (the importer's own description).

opensIn.note: Imports InDesign IDML and IDMS (since 1.5.0). It converts InDesign objects into Scribus page items; not every object type is supported.

adobe-indesign.tip: Check fonts, images and page layout after import. Opensource.com's 2018 test found simple files fine and a book layout lost some styling (secondhand; not verified here).

export: Your documents are already PDF files, so they open in any PDF app as they are.
For editable copies, choose Convert in the top bar, pick Word, Excel or PowerPoint, then Convert and save.
To take only part, select text, right-click and choose Export Selection As.
formats: DOCX, DOC, XLSX, RTF, XML, HTML, CSV (converted copies)
wontComeOver: Converting PDF to Word or Excel in Acrobat requires a paid Export PDF subscription when done from Reader.

export: Open the design and click Share, then Download.
Pick a file type: PDF, PNG, SVG, or PPTX (presentations only).
Click Download.
wontComeOver: PPTX can look different in PowerPoint; fonts may need installing.
Transparent PNG and SVG need a paid Canva plan.
A flattened PDF cannot be edited easily.

opensIn.note: Penpot's data model notes it can import SVG files, rebuilding elements as shapes with a best-effort guess for files not made in Penpot.

canva.tip: SVG is the choice that stays editable as shapes.

export: Open the chat, then More options, More, Export chat.
Choose Without media or Include media.
Pick where to send it (email or another app). It arrives as a .txt file.
formats: Text file (.txt) with optional recent media
wontComeOver: An exported chat is a text file and cannot be re-imported to restore the chat.
With media, only the latest 10,000 messages are sent; without media, 40,000.
Export is not a backup; WhatsApp's backup is separate.
whatsapp.tip: None of the listed alternatives' docs that I could check say they import WhatsApp chats.

export: Open User Settings and go to the Privacy section to request your data.
Choose the categories you want (desktop or browser only; mobile requests everything).
Wait for the email with a download link, then download the ZIP.
wontComeOver: It can take up to 30 days.
Files are JSON and open in a basic text editor, not in another chat app.
Your account must be email-verified, and the request is cancelled if you disable or delete the account before the link arrives.

export: Log in at dropbox.com and tick the files or folders you want.
Click Download. Folders arrive as .zip files.
For a big library, use the Dropbox desktop app to sync a full copy to your computer.
wontComeOver: A folder over 250 GB or with 10,000+ files cannot be downloaded from the website.

export: Go to iCloud.com/photos on a computer and select up to 1,000 items.
Click Download and choose Unmodified Originals, Highest Resolution, or Most Compatible.
On iPhone or iPad you can use Export Unmodified Originals in Photos.
wontComeOver: You cannot export iCloud photos while Advanced Data Protection is on.
Selection is capped at 1,000 items per download.
icloud-photos.tip: Apple also has a request page at privacy.apple.com for a full data copy (Apple Support 118257 and 102283).

export: Go to iCloud.com and open iCloud Drive.
Select the file and click Download. It lands in your downloads folder.
wontComeOver: You cannot export while Advanced Data Protection is on (Apple's iCloud data pages).

export: Open a project, click the three-dots icon at the top right, choose Manage data, then Export as CSV.
For everything at once, go to Settings, then Backups, and download a backup (a ZIP with one CSV per active project).
wontComeOver: Completed tasks are left out of project CSV exports and backups; archived projects are skipped in backups.
Todoist's own CSV import is limited to 300 tasks per project.

opensIn.note: Has a Todoist migrator (Settings, Import from other services), but your Vikunja must be reachable from the internet and you create a Todoist developer app to link them.

export: Cloud recordings: open Recordings in the Zoom web portal and download the files.
Meeting chat saved to the cloud: after processing, download the TXT chat file from the Recordings page.
Account owners can download Chat History reports as CSV or HTML (Reports, User activity reports, Chat history).
wontComeOver: Cloud chat only holds messages sent to everyone; private messages are not saved there.
Chat History downloads are deleted after 30 days.
I found no single Zoom page for a full account export.

export: Go to takeout.google.com and tick Saved (your lists of places).
Choose a destination, frequency and file type, then create the export.
Wait for the email with the link.
wontComeOver: Google's Maps page does not say what file format the saved places arrive in.

opensIn.note: Imports bookmarks and tracks in KML, KMZ, KMB, GPX and GeoJSON, including from third-party apps. Open the file with the app, or import a whole folder from the bookmarks screen.

google-maps.tip: Check what format Takeout gives you; Organic Maps only reads the formats listed.

export: Go to takeout.google.com and select only Keep.
Create the export and download it from the email link.
wontComeOver: Deleted notes are not in the export.
Work or school accounts may have some data unavailable.
google-keep.tip: Includes text, attachments, colour, pinned or archived status, collaborators and labels, per Google. Joplin's import page does not list Keep.

export: Recordings and transcripts are saved in the organizer's Google Drive, in a Google Meet folder.
Select the file in Drive, then More, then Download.
Chat is saved as a separate .SBV file in the same place.
wontComeOver: Transcripts hold only spoken words, not chat messages.
Only the organizer's Drive receives them.

export: Open the form and go to the Responses tab.
Click More, then Download responses (.csv).
wontComeOver: The page describes exporting responses, not the form's questions.
With over 10,000 responses the CSV may not be sorted by time.

export: In a browser go to reddit.com/settings/data-request and log in.
Follow the instructions and submit the form.
Reddit sends a download link to your inbox (or verified email), up to 30 days later.
formats: CSV files (posts.csv, comments.csv, messages.csv, subscribed_subreddits.csv and more)
wontComeOver: Your posts and comments leave as spreadsheets; none of the listed alternatives' docs I checked say they import them.
reddit.tip: Posts, comments and votes can also be viewed in your account at any time, per Reddit.

export: Go to takeout.google.com and sign in. Keep only YouTube ticked.
Choose how to receive it and a file type, then Create export.
Download from the email link when it is ready.
wontComeOver: Takeout does not download other people's videos.
The download link expires after about 7 days.
youtube.tip: The Google Takeout help page does not say which YouTube formats arrive; I did not find an alternative's page that imports them.

export: Go to netflix.com/account/getmyinfo and follow the instructions to request your personal information.
For viewing history only: on the Viewing activity page for a profile, use the download option at the bottom for a CSV.
wontComeOver: The full request can take up to 30 days.
Profile users who added their own email must email privacy@netflix.com, and the account owner is notified.

export: On the Goodreads website (not the mobile app) open My Books.
Under Tools choose Import and export, then Export Library.
When it finishes, click the dated link to download the .csv.
formats: CSV (your library); full account data as a ZIP of JSON files
wontComeOver: Mobile often cannot save the export link; use the desktop site.
Goodreads' full data download is JSON, a different format from the library CSV.

opensIn.note: The Goodreads importer reads your exported shelf file into Reading Logs, but only for titles in Open Library's catalog that have ISBNs.

goodreads.tip: That Open Library note is from a 2020 blog post; check it still works.

export: Open your privacy settings and select Submit Request next to Personal Data Report.
Wait for the email (usually a few hours), then re-enter your credentials to view it. Access lasts seven days.
wontComeOver: Grammarly says documents stored in your account can be downloaded by following its Help Center steps; I did not find those steps.

export: Go to Audience, click Export audience, then Export CSV (Owners and Admins only). You can export a segment or tag.
For campaign numbers: Campaigns, View report, Actions, Export CSV.
For everything: Account, Settings, Manage my data.
formats: CSV; possibly a ZIP with a CSV per contact type (subscribed, unsubscribed, non-subscribed, cleaned)
wontComeOver: Contact exports do not include campaign performance data.
Exports stay available for 30 days.
Standard campaign reports leave out per-subscriber opens and clicks.

opensIn.note: Imports contacts from CSV (Import Contacts on the Contacts page). A Replace duplicates checkbox updates existing contacts. Custom data is stored as JSON, not CSV columns.

mailchimp.tip: Import the audience CSV and keep unsubscribed and cleaned contacts out of your new list.

export: Open the form and go to Results, then Responses.
Tick the checkbox in the header row (or select particular responses), then click the Export icon.
Choose CSV or XLSX; it downloads and is also emailed.
wontComeOver: The form's questions and design are not part of a responses export.
Yes/No answers appear as 1 and 0.
Multiple-selection answers split into one column per choice.
You cannot export from the mobile builder.

export: Go to the Meetings page and filter the meetings you want.
Click Export at the top right.
The CSV downloads or arrives by email.
formats: CSV (invitee details, event type, date, location, UTM and payment data)
wontComeOver: There is no direct export of the Contacts list; export past meetings instead (a Calendly community answer).

export: Open the poll from your dashboard, click More, then Export (closed polls: the three dots next to it, then Export).
The Excel file lands in your Downloads folder.
wontComeOver: Export is a paid feature (Pro, Team or Enterprise).

export: Go to Settings, then the Security and apps tab.
Click Download your information.
Medium emails a link to a .zip of HTML files.
wontComeOver: The export includes comments you wrote on other stories, which Ghost may import as posts; check the result.

opensIn.note: Has a Medium migrator in Ghost Admin that imports posts and subscribers (subscribers come from Medium's audience stats list export).

export: In your publication go to Settings, then Exports.
Create a new export; Substack builds a zip with posts, subscriber list and stats.
For subscribers only: Subscribers page, three-dot menu, export CSV.
formats: ZIP of posts and subscriber CSVs
wontComeOver: Subscriber names are not currently included in the export.
Paid subscribers need the same Stripe account connected to move billing.

opensIn.note: Built-in Substack importer in Ghost Admin (Settings, Advanced, Import/Export): upload the content zip, then separate free and paid subscriber CSVs. Forum users report problems on messy exports.

export: On the web go to Settings, then Data Controls, then Export.
Confirm. You get an email or SMS when it is ready.
Download the ZIP within 24 hours.
formats: ZIP with chat history and account data
wontComeOver: The link expires 24 hours after you receive it.
Deleted chats cannot be restored from an export.
Not available for Business or Enterprise accounts.

export: Code: on the repository page click Code, copy the URL, and run git clone in a terminal (or gh repo clone OWNER/REPO).
Issues, labels, wiki, releases and milestones are copied by the new host's migration tool, not by cloning.
wontComeOver: Cloning copies code only, not issues or the wiki.
Codeberg's guide does not say whether pull requests migrate.

opensIn.note: Migration tool (New Migration, choose GitHub) copies issues, labels, wiki, releases and milestones. A GitHub access token is needed for metadata or private repositories; delete the token afterwards. Steps are from Codeberg's guide, which runs Forgejo.

export: In the Dashlane web app open My account, then Settings, then Export Data.
Choose Export to CSV and save the file. You get a zip with several CSV files.
wontComeOver: CSV files are not encrypted; delete them after importing.
Passkeys cannot be exported to CSV, and 2FA tokens cannot be exported directly to CSV.
On iPhone, iPad and Mac (26 and later) Credential Exchange can move passwords, passkeys and codes without a file; it does not work on Android.

opensIn.note: Imports Dashlane CSV (or legacy JSON). Run the import once per CSV file. It does not check for duplicates, so importing twice doubles items. Attachments must be re-added by hand.

export: Authy does not offer an export button, and its desktop apps no longer allow exporting.
Workarounds need a rooted Android phone, or an iPhone plus a computer and technical tools (Ente's migration guide).
Otherwise, set up two-step login again on each account in the new app.
formats: Plain text or Bitwarden-format JSON, via the workarounds
wontComeOver: The workarounds may not export every code; check each account before removing Authy.
Exported files contain unencrypted secrets; delete them after migrating.
This is not an Authy-supported route.

opensIn.note: Imports codes from a plain-text or Bitwarden-format JSON file (menu, Data, Import codes), or by scanning QR codes.

authy.tip: Authy's own help page could not be checked; the facts here come from Ente's guide and 2FAS support.

export: Open Telegram Desktop (the web version cannot export).
Go to Settings, then Advanced, then Export Telegram data. For one chat use its menu, then Export chat history.
Choose HTML (readable) or JSON.
wontComeOver: If you just logged in on Desktop, you may have to wait 24 hours or confirm from another device.
A 2024 bug report said HTML exports of some old group messages came out blank; JSON did not.

export: On a computer click the Me icon, then Settings & Privacy, then Data Privacy.
Choose Get a copy of your data, pick the categories (or the larger archive), and request it.
Download from the email link: small requests in minutes, the full archive within 24 hours; the link works for 72 hours.
wontComeOver: Not available on mobile.
People You May Know and Who's Viewed Your Profile data are not included.
Connection email addresses may be missing if the connection hid them.
linkedin.tip: Closing your account cuts off access to the data, so download first.

export: In the app go to your data settings and tap Download your data.
Choose what to include and a file format, then tap Request data.
Download it within the few days it stays available (up to 4 days).
wontComeOver: Preparation may take a few days.

export: Go to Settings, then Privacy and data, then Request your data, and tap Start request.
Within about 48 hours Pinterest emails a download link (sent through SendSafely).
wontComeOver: Pinterest's page does not say what file format the data arrives in.

export: No file export is needed for Baserow: create a public share link to the whole base in Airtable.
In Baserow choose Add new, then Database, then the Import from Airtable tab, and paste the link.
wontComeOver: Formula, lookup, rollup, collaborator, created-by and button fields are not imported (convert them to text or number first).
Automations, interfaces, integrations, comments and access controls must be rebuilt.
Baserow adds an 'Airtable import report' table listing what was skipped.

opensIn.note: Built-in Airtable importer from a public share link: tables, most field types, links between tables, attachments and grid views carry over.

airtable.tip: These steps are from Baserow's page; I did not verify Airtable's own export steps.

export: Open the file, then Main menu, File, Save local copy to download a .fig file.
Or export your designs as SVG files in a zip.
wontComeOver: Penpot cannot open .fig files directly.
If you do not see Save local copy, the owner may have restricted copying.

opensIn.note: No direct .fig import. Penpot's blog describes a Figma plugin that exports a zip you import through Import Penpot Files (not fully reliable), or SVG files exported from Figma that you import from the Projects menu.

figma.tip: Penpot's blog calls the plugin imperfect; one community report says large files crashed Penpot.

export: No file export is needed for Plane: create a Personal Access Token in Asana.
In Plane use its Asana importer, pick the workspace and project, and map sections to states.
wontComeOver: Asana issue types become labels or title prefixes in Plane.

opensIn.note: Asana importer brings labels, users, work items, comments, attachments and parent-child links, and can re-run to sync later changes.

asana.tip: Steps come from Plane's docs; I did not find Asana's own export page.

export: No file export is needed for Plane: you need an API token, your email and your Jira site URL.
In Plane use its Jira importer; add a JQL filter to limit which issues come over.
wontComeOver: Jira issue types become Plane work item types only if Work Item Types is enabled first.
Sprints become cycles; epics become an ordinary work item type.

opensIn.note: Imports from Jira Cloud and Jira Server/Data Center.

jira.tip: Steps come from Plane's docs; I did not find Jira's own export page.

export: In Shopify admin go to Products and click Export.
Choose all products, the current page, selected items or filtered results.
Pick a CSV for spreadsheets or a plain CSV, and export.
wontComeOver: Shopify lists each variant on its own row; WooCommerce uses a parent product with variation rows, so the file needs restructuring.
Shopify-only columns such as Handle or Vendor may need removing.

opensIn.note: Has a built-in CSV product importer (WooCommerce, Products, Import) with column mapping. WooCommerce's migration guide advises backing up first and testing with a small file.

shopify.tip: A user reported images did not populate after a Shopify CSV import (secondhand search result).

export: Log in at accounts.snapchat.com or open Settings, then My Data in the app.
Pick the categories and a date range (or turn the range off for everything).
Confirm your email and click Submit; download the zip from the email link or the My Data page.
wontComeOver: Snapchat aims to deliver within 7 days; large downloads take longer.
A data request cannot be cancelled.

export: Use Meta's Export Your Information tool and choose Messenger.
Pick HTML (easy to read) or JSON (easier to move to another service), plus categories and a date range.
Download the ZIP within 4 days of it being ready.
wontComeOver: End-to-end encrypted chats are downloaded separately, from their own Messenger help page.
The file is a ZIP with an index you open in a browser; none of the listed alternatives' docs I checked import it.
